headline: Alaska Senate: Judge fast tracks new bids to dismiss DOJ lawsuit over 2nd Sullivan candidacy
author: Dan Mangan

paragraphs.text: A federal judge in Alaska on Friday kept on a fast track motions to dismiss the Department of Justice's lawsuit that seeks to delay certification of the state's Senate election.

Judge Sharon Gleason ordered the DOJ to respond by 1 p.m. Alaska Time Friday to the new dismissal motions, which were filed hours after the DOJ amended its complaint in U.S. District Court in Anchorage on Thursday.
Gleason gave state election officials, the campaign of Democratic nominee Mary Peltola, and other groups until noon Saturday to reply to the DOJ's response.

The DOJ's suit seeks to delay certification of the Senate election if incumbent Republican Sen. Dan Sullivan loses by a margin that could be attributable to voter confusion over the presence of another candidate named Dan Sullivan on the ballot.

The judge's order leaves open the possibility that she will rule on the dismissal motions before Tuesday, which is Election Day. The state and Peltola's campaign have asked Gleason to dismiss the case before then.
The winner of Alaska's race could determine which party holds a majority in the Senate in January. Republicans currently have 53 seats in the 100-member chamber.
